1oru2l5:260: Claude Code's design philosophy is to treat "failure will definitely happen" as a design premise, not as an exception. The core mechanism of StreamingToolExecutor is: during the model's streaming output, as soon as a tool_use JSON block is detected, tool execution starts immediately without waiting for the model to finish speaking ^. Read-only operations run up to 10 in parallel, write operations are queued serially ^. More critically, the "tombstone message" mechanism: when the API is interrupted, an error placeholder is generated for every orphaned tool call, and the interruption message is marked as TombstoneMessage, ensuring the message stream never breaks ^. This design does not aim to eliminate failure, but to keep the system state intact and debuggable in the face of faults ^.

The key innovation of L3 Context Collapse is that the collapse operation is reversible and auditable: the commit log records raw data, and projectView() can replay it ^. Most frameworks compress destructively; Claude Code chose a more complex implementation to preserve debugging capability ^. This is directly related to the "dynamic system evaluation" among the three research directions proposed by Dario Amodei — long-term planning, multi-agent coordination, and dynamic system evaluation — because when you need to evaluate an agent system, you first need to be able to trace back to what happened at each step ^.
bn1691:221: Claude Code's memory solution is Markdown + YAML frontmatter, not a vector database ^. The underlying logic of this choice is: vector matching solves lexical similarity, but cannot compute the semantic connection between "last time we said don't mock the database" and "now we need to write database tests" ^. A small model (inferring from 5 file headers) has extremely low cost, yet captures this precise task-context association ^. The Feedback mechanism records both "corrections" and "confirmations" — learning only from mistakes makes the agent increasingly conservative, so recording what was done right prevents regression ^.
